fork.name: PNW Pilot
fork.description: A personal production distribution of openpilot built on the xnor-tech fork for its legacy Tesla (Raven) support and tuned for the Pacific Northwest I-5 corridor. It serves exactly two daily-driven cars — a 2021 Tesla Model S (Raven, HW3) and a 2025 Ford F-150 Lightning — with one comma 3X moved between them, layering a chill-by-default curve-anticipating longitudinal stack (CES/VTSC/MTSC/ICBM), BluePilot-derived Ford lateral control, self-hosted uploads, and OSM map services on top. Safety posture: new toggles default OFF, panda safety is never weakened, and car-specific code is capability-gated so each car is inert to the other's features.

features.name: openpilot Longitudinal Control
features.description: openpilot controls gas and brake instead of the car's stock adaptive cruise. Native on some cars; on many others it is available only behind the Alpha Longitudinal toggle. On this fork the Tesla Model S Raven runs it always-on, while the F-150 Lightning has an opt-in Alpha toggle (off = stock Ford ACC).

features.name: Experimental Mode (end-to-end longitudinal)
features.description: End-to-end driving mode that slows for curves, stop lights and stop signs using the driving model. Requires openpilot longitudinal control; availability follows each car's oplong status. This fork mostly drives Chill and lets CES switch into Experimental automatically.

features.name: Driver Monitoring
features.description: Infrared camera-based driver attention monitoring with escalating alerts. Always active on every car; this fork ships the newer sleep-probability DM model from upstream.

features.name: Automated Lane Centering
features.description: Continuous lane centering steering on highways and city streets. Works on all supported cars; some models have a minimum steering speed.

features.name: Lane Change Assist
features.description: Signal and nudge the wheel and openpilot completes the lane change. Standard openpilot behavior on all supported cars.

features.name: Stop and Go
features.description: Follows traffic down to a complete stop and resumes automatically. Depends on the car's ACC hardware; some cars cannot accelerate from a stop or below a minimum speed.

features.name: Model Confidence Ball
features.description: A comma-four-style indicator ball on the right edge of the screen showing the driving model's own confidence in its current plan (green high, amber mid, red low). Display-only; ported via sunnypilot.

features.name: Vision Turn Speed Control
features.description: Caps cruise speed through curves based on the driving model's predicted path curvature, with a gentle regen-style decel envelope and a highway speed-limit floor. Lineage: Move Fast team via sunnypilot; this fork's own implementation rides the CES master toggle and requires openpilot longitudinal. Tuned only on the fork's two cars.

features.name: Map Turn Speed Control (map-curve braking)
features.description: Folds OpenStreetMap curve speeds (pfeiferj mapd) into VTSC so the car brakes for sharp curves the camera cannot see yet, scanning the full ~500 m map horizon and timing the slowdown so the curve entrance is the slowest point. Default ON when CES is enabled; requires openpilot longitudinal.

features.name: ICBM — stock-ACC curve slowdowns via cruise buttons
features.description: When openpilot longitudinal is off, steers the car's own ACC set speed toward a curve target by pressing its SET-/SET+ cruise buttons over CAN — curve anticipation without taking longitudinal authority. Concept invented by sunnypilot, Ford port by BluePilot; this fork re-implements it for the F-150 Lightning only.

features.name: Green Light / Lead Departure Alert
features.description: A chime and green banner when a held stop releases with no lead ('Light is green'), and a separate note when a close stopped lead pulls away. Always on for both cars; mechanics adopted from sunnypilot with FrogPilot's stop-context arming.

features.name: No Disengage on Brake
features.description: Would keep openpilot engaged through a brake tap. The toggle exists in this fork but is marked unsupported and greyed out — braking still disengages.

features.name: Ford 4-signal (BlueCruise-grade) lateral
features.description: Ports BluePilot's validated 4-signal steer command (curvature + curvature rate + path offset + path angle) with matching hardened panda safety, giving noticeably stronger steering than the stock 2-signal path. Requires a panda reflash; capability-gated to the F-150 Lightning, Tesla safety untouched.

features.name: Ford angle-primary lateral (experimental)
features.description: A faithful port of Alan Polk's BluePilot bp-7.0 angle-primary steering control for Ford, behind the FordAngleLateral driver toggle (default OFF, experimental). Actively being tuned with a curve-triggered logger; gain anchors confirmed by the original author.

features.name: Ford highway follow control (LongitudinalExt)
features.description: BluePilot's lead-follow shaping — classifies the lead as gaining/pacing/trailing and shapes gas and brake per state with a highway speed deadband. Ships in the tree for the Lightning but stays dormant until the Alpha Longitudinal toggle is on.

features.name: BlueCruise cluster display + rich cluster messaging
features.description: The Ford factory instrument cluster shows the blue BlueCruise engaged state when openpilot is steering, plus openpilot status messages (Cancelled, lane departure, etc.) rendered in the cluster. Display-only, no reflash needed; Lightning-specific.

features.name: CES — Conditional Experimental Switching
features.description: Chill mode stays the default and the car auto-switches into Experimental only for upcoming curves (map + vision), low speed, stop lights and slow leads, with red-light stop-hold guards, standstill latch, lead-pacing and merge/accel-zone gates. 3-state on-screen button (CES/Chill/Exp). Concept from FrogPilot's Conditional Experimental Mode, independently implemented; opt-in (CESMode default Off) and requires openpilot longitudinal; tuned on real I-5/I-90 drive logs.

features.name: Nudgeless Lane Change
features.description: After the blinker is on for a short hold, the lane change starts without a steering nudge. Opt-in toggle, default OFF; wired only for the fork's two cars (Tesla Raven + F-150 Lightning), with the Tesla's blind-spot state available to block a change into an occupied lane.

features.name: Self-hosted connect + two-pass uploads
features.description: Drives upload to the owner's own AWS S3 gateway instead of comma connect: pass 1 (logs) on any network, pass 2 (HD video/rlog) only on real WiFi and offroad, HD-interleave, Defer-HD toggle, upload-phase sidebar indicators with Mbps, failed-upload surfacing, and a device locator that reports the car's LAN IP on every upload.

features.name: 'Happening Ahead' overlay (police / rest areas / EV chargers)
features.description: A display-only overlay merging live Waze police reports (keyless caching proxy), curated corridor rest-area data, and EV DC-fast chargers (opt-in L2) ahead on your route. Never affects steering or speed; on by default on any car.

features.name: DM road-gated timeouts + glare desensitization
features.description: A 3-way DmMode selector (Default stock-strict / Highway-relaxed only on freeways via map data / Relaxed) with personal timeout magnitudes kept device-local, plus glare handling that keeps DM active through low-sun glare bursts instead of nagging. Monitoring itself is never disabled.

features.name: Perpetual tethering + priority WiFi + captive portal
features.description: Keeps the device hotspot up, auto-joins known priority WiFi networks only near saved home locations (GPS-gated), auto-accepts captive portals (MikroTik/OSU variants), and guards against LTE throttling with a NAT fix for tethered clients. Works on any car.

features.name: Rain mode curve slowdown
features.description: Driver-selected wet-weather margin subtracted from curve target speeds (Light ~3 mph, Heavy ~5 mph) without touching the dry tuning. Applies wherever the fork's curve control (VTSC/CES) is active; default None.

features.name: Auto-recalibrate on car swap
features.description: When the comma device is moved to a different car, the learned camera calibration and per-car steering parameters are cleared automatically before the next drive — no manual Reset Calibration. Same-car reboots are untouched; pairs with fingerprint hardening so a swap can never show the wrong car.

features.name: Blind-spot monitoring gate (Tesla Raven)
features.description: Reads the Tesla Raven's own blind-spot state from the Autopilot status CAN message, logs it and uses it to block nudgeless lane changes into an occupied lane. Deployed but the physical walk-by flip test is still pending; Tesla Raven only.

features.name: OSM map data (pfeiferj mapd)
features.description: pfeiferj/mapd v2 provides OpenStreetMap speed limits, road names and curve speeds. Map data for Washington, Oregon and Idaho auto-downloads on first launch; other regions downloadable on demand ('Get map for this location'). Feeds MTSC and the on-screen speed-limit display.

features.name: Road name + speed limit display
features.description: Shows the current road name and posted speed limit from OSM on screen, with a warning styling when driving over the limit. Display-only on every car.

features.name: Legacy Tesla (pre-AP/AP1/Raven) support
features.description: Full legacy Tesla support inherited from the xnor-tech base: tesla_legacy panda safety, legacy CAN stack, Continental radar and ignition detection for pre-refresh Model S/X — cars stock openpilot dropped. This is the reason the fork builds on xnor. Only the 2021 Model S Raven HW3 is actually driven and validated.

cars.note: The fork's second daily driver (2025 Flash, 131 kWh).
